title: Imperative (commands)
summary: The imperative gives orders, instructions and advice. Take the tu, nous or vous form of the present tense and drop the subject pronoun: Finis ! Écoutons ! Prenez !
-er verbs, aller, and verbs like ouvrir and offrir (tu ouvres, tu offres) drop the -s of the tu form: tu regardes → Regarde ! tu vas → Va ! tu ouvres → Ouvre !
The -s comes back before y and en: Vas-y ! Achètes-en !
The nous form means 'let's': Partons ! Allons au cinéma !
Irregular forms: être → sois, soyons, soyez; avoir → aie, ayons, ayez. Also recognise savoir → sache, sachez and vouloir → veuillez (Veuillez patienter = Please wait).
Negative commands: ne ... pas goes round the verb: Ne crie pas ! Ne courez pas !
Positive commands: object and reflexive pronouns go after the verb with a hyphen, and me/te become moi/toi: Lève-toi ! Regarde-moi ! Prends-le !
With two pronouns in a positive command, the direct object comes first: Donne-le-moi ! Envoie-la-moi !
Negative commands: the pronouns go back in front of the verb in their normal form: Ne te lève pas ! Ne le prends pas !

cards.front: How do you form the imperative (a command)?
cards.back: Use the tu, nous or vous form of the present tense without the pronoun: tu finis → Finis ! nous partons → Partons ! (Let's leave!) vous écoutez → Écoutez ! -er verbs drop the -s in the tu form: tu regardes → Regarde !

cards.en: Are you thirsty? Drink some water!
cards.why: The tu form of boire in the present (tu bois) without the pronoun: Bois !

cards.prompt: Paul, ___ la porte, s'il te plaît !
cards.why: fermer is an -er verb, so the tu command drops the -s: tu fermes → Ferme !

cards.prompt: Les enfants, ___ vos devoirs avant de jouer !
cards.en: Children, finish your homework before you play!
cards.why: Speaking to several people, so use the vous form without the pronoun: Finissez !

cards.prompt: Il fait beau : ___ au parc cet après-midi !
cards.en: It's sunny: let's go to the park this afternoon!
cards.why: The nous form of the imperative means 'let's': Allons !

cards.front: When does the tu imperative drop its -s, and when does it keep it?
cards.back: -er verbs, aller, and verbs like ouvrir, offrir and découvrir (whose tu form ends in -es) drop the -s: tu manges → Mange ! tu vas → Va ! tu ouvres → Ouvre ! Other verbs keep it: Finis ! Prends ! Fais ! The -s comes back before y or en so that it is easier to say: Vas-y ! Manges-en !

cards.instruction: Turn the sentence into a command.
cards.why: ouvrir has -er-type endings in the present (tu ouvres), so, like an -er verb, it drops the -s in the tu command: Ouvre.

cards.prompt: Tu veux aller à la piscine ? Alors ___-y !
cards.en: You want to go to the swimming pool? Then go!
cards.why: Va ! normally has no -s, but before y the -s comes back for the sound: Vas-y !

cards.back: être: sois, soyons, soyez (Sois sage ! = Be good!). avoir: aie, ayons, ayez (N'aie pas peur ! = Don't be afraid!). To recognise: savoir → sache, sachons, sachez; vouloir → veuillez, used in polite notices: Veuillez fermer la porte = Please close the door.

cards.why: être has an irregular imperative: sois (tu), soyons (nous), soyez (vous). ta shows it is the tu form.

cards.prompt: ___ confiance en toi : tu vas réussir !
cards.en: Have confidence in yourself: you're going to succeed!
cards.why: avoir has an irregular imperative: aie (tu), ayons (nous), ayez (vous). toi shows it is the tu form.

cards.front: Where do the pronouns go in reflexive commands with vous and nous, positive and negative?
cards.back: Positive: after the verb, joined by a hyphen: Reposez-vous ! Habillons-nous ! Negative: back in front of the verb, inside ne ... pas: Ne vous disputez pas ! Ne nous énervons pas ! With tu, te becomes toi only in a positive command: Habille-toi ! but Ne t'habille pas ! Object pronouns follow the same pattern: Prenez-le ! / Ne le prenez pas !

cards.prompt: Les enfants, ___ vite : votre bus arrive dans cinq minutes !
cards.en: Children, get dressed quickly: your bus comes in five minutes!
cards.why: Speaking to several children (votre bus), so use the vous form. In a positive command the reflexive pronoun goes after the verb with a hyphen: habillez-vous.
nous imperative of a reflexive verb: the pronoun nous follows the verb with a hyphen: Dépêchons-nous !

answers: Ne nous couchons pas tard ce soir !
cards.en: Let's not go to bed late tonight!
cards.why: In a negative command the reflexive pronoun goes back in front of the verb, and ne ... pas goes round the pronoun and the verb together: Ne nous couchons pas.

cards.instruction: Replace the words in bold with a pronoun.
cards.en: Let's invite her to the party!
cards.why: Sarah is a feminine direct object, so la. In a positive command it goes after the verb, joined by a hyphen: Invitons-la.

answers: Ne lui téléphonez pas ce soir !
cards.why: In a negative command the pronoun goes back in front of the verb, and ne ... pas goes round both: Ne lui téléphonez pas.

cards.instruction: Replace the words in bold with a pronoun.
cards.why: vos photos becomes les. With two pronouns after a positive command, the direct object comes first and all the parts are joined by hyphens: Montrez-les-moi !
